thread:
carla_support: ACME support ticket: multiple customers in eu-west are seeing p99 jump for embeddings and chat + intermittent 401s during high load. Started ~15:10 UTC after our maintenance window. Billing retries also increased. Can we triage?

alice_sre: Thanks — are there logs or a repro? Any recent deploys or infra changes in that window?

carla_support: They attached traces. Quick snippet from our API proxy (customer-side):
```
2026-03-16T15:12:08Z ERROR request=abcd auth=401 duration=2053ms route=/v1/embeddings model=text-embed-3
2026-03-16T15:12:09Z WARN request=abce backend=timeout tok_refresh=failed
```
User reports 401s during token refresh and timeouts at p99 ~2s on generation calls (was ~120ms).

infra-monitor-bot: [ALERT] eu-west cluster: hostfs_io_wait p95/p99 increased 4x since 15:08 UTC. NVMe qdepth > 128 on several nodes.

bob_infra: I'm seeing simultaneous driver/kernel updates rolled out to eu-west during the maintenance window — CUDA runtime 12.3.x + driver 540.x on the prod-gpu pool. Rolling update started 15:05 UTC. Correlates with the spike.

emma_runtime: Can you paste node-level iostat / dstat? Also any kernel patches applied? We saw increased KV cache flush times in earlier rollouts.

bob_infra: quick paste:
```
node-12 iostat: nvme0 tps=4500  read_ms=18.2  wait_ms=7.1  util=94%
node-13 iostat: nvme0 tps=4220  read_ms=21.5  wait_ms=9.8  util=96%
sysstat: disk-queue depth: avg 110 -> spike 260
```
Looks like hostfs/host kernel interactions driving NVMe contention.

frank_ml: From model side, we also saw a KV cache miss storm — many sessions reloaded their KV caches simultaneously. If host NVMe slows, cache warmup becomes very expensive and amplifies tail.

alice_sre: That explains the 401s during token refresh? Token service calls started taking longer and sometimes timed out, client retried and hit auth rate limits. Combined effect = 401s & billing retry churn.

carla_support: Customer-facing: "Our app's search experience is timing out intermittently and users are seeing errors" — they'd like ETA and mitigation.

emma_runtime: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) Rollback driver/CUDA on a small subset and test; 2) Route new requests away from eu-west to eu-north fallback for affected tenants; 3) Increase token service timeouts and add jitter to refresh to avoid stampeding.

alice_sre: I'll coordinate rollback with bob. Bob can you pause the rollout and start a rollback to driver 535.x on a canary subset?

bob_infra: Paused rollout at 15:23 UTC. Starting rollback on canary nodes (node-12,node-15). Command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout undo daemonset/gpu-drivers --to-revision=535 -l region=eu-west
```
ETA for canary rollback ~6-8m.

deploy-bot: Rollback job submitted: job_id=rb-20260316-01 status=queued.

alice_sre: In parallel, can we throttle token refresh per-user and add backoff in the auth gateway? If we reduce refresh blast to 1/5th we probably remove auth storms.

frank_ml: Also enabling a temporary in-memory KV cache fallback on runtime nodes for active sessions will reduce NVMe reads. I can push a feature flag for that.

bob_infra: Canary nodes show nvme util dropping to 56% after rollback. Early signal looks good.

infra-monitor-bot: [INFO] node-12 nvme util -> 54%  p99 latency for disk ops down 3x after rollback on canary.

carla_support: Customer update drafted: "We're diagnosing an infrastructure regression introduced during today's maintenance. We've isolated the issue to a storage/driver interaction and are rolling back a recent driver update; we'll follow up with timeline. Apologies for the disruption." Want me to send?

dan_custsuccess: Please send, include that we're routing traffic and applying mitigations now. Keep tone: we're on it, ETA under 1 hour for broader recovery.

grace_product: After stabilizing, we should consider making driver rollouts staged by qdepth and add automatic rollback when hostfs qdepth > threshold. Filing a product ask.

emma_runtime: Action list (short):
- bob: finish rollback across eu-west + verify nvme qdepth stabilization
- alice: throttle token refresh, raise auth gateway timeouts + retries
- frank: enable in-memory KV fallback flag for warm sessions
- carla/dan: customer comms + monitor
- grace: track product follow-up (postmortem + rollout gating)

alice_sre: I'm increasing auth gateway timeout from 1s -> 5s and adding jittered backoff for refresh:
```json
{"refresh_backoff_ms": [100, 350, 1200], "max_attempts": 3}
```
Pushing now.

deploy-bot: auth-gateway rollout started: deploy_id=dg-20260316-42 status=ok

bob_infra: eu-west rollback complete across 12/12 nodes at 15:48 UTC. NVMe util normalized. Monitoring for 30m.

infra-monitor-bot: [RECOVERY] eu-west hostfs_io_wait p99 returned to baseline.

carla_support: Sent customer update: initial mitigation complete; we'll keep them posted with a postmortem.

dan_custsuccess: Customer acknowledged and appreciates quick response. They've asked for a short timeline for root cause and a follow-up review.

grace_product: Who owns the postmortem? Alice/bob/frank team?

alice_sre: I'll own the incident write-up and coordinate with bob/frank for infra/model pieces. Expect draft in 24h.

emma_runtime: Follow-ups: add gating for driver rollouts (qdepth & io metrics), add token refresh throttling as a platform default, and add cache-warmup strategies to avoid simultaneous KV reloads.

carla_support: Closing thread for now; will re-open if we see regression. Thanks all :thumbsup:
